observation: Whole set in the opening position, all three views inspected. TOP: the 7x9 field is complete and mirror-symmetric -- a den flanked by three traps at each end (black den with cyan traps at the Anti end, tan den with orange traps at the Sol end), the twelve asteroid-belt tiles as two 2x3 blocks either side of the centre file, and sixteen worlds each centred on its own cell, eight on white discs and eight on black. No piece straddles a cell boundary, no tile sits proud of its pocket, and the two storage trays are clear of the board. FRONT: every piece stands on the board top with its disc fully landed; the size ladder reads correctly left to right with Jupiter the largest globe and Mars and Earth the smallest; Saturn's ring is a near-level brim and Uranus's is an upright hoop, which is the designed difference; the two corona flame cones rise from their own tiles and touch nothing. ISO: no floating geometry, no part passing through another, no missing or duplicated piece. Neptune's royal-blue globes carry their three white bands, the dark spot and the new small bright companion oval below it; at this whole-set framing the companion is near the limit of what the frame resolves, which is expected for a 1.9 x 1.0 mm marking on a 21.9 mm globe and is why the per-world frames under snap/worlds/ carry it. Counted 222 occurrences in the assembly package, two more than the published set, and the two are exactly the new companion bodies.
